# SSGOI - Page Transition Library

> Universal page transition library that works in all browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari), unlike the View Transition API (Chrome-only).

This document is for AI assistants to help developers set up SSGOI page transitions.

**Per-transition reference (options, data keys, examples):** see the `Transitions` section below — each entry links to its own page like `https://ssgoi.dev/llms/<name>.txt`.

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install @ssgoi/react
# or @ssgoi/svelte, @ssgoi/vue, @ssgoi/solid, @ssgoi/angular
```

---

## Layout Setup

SSGOI works on any web app. There are only three things to get right:

1. **Decide your scroll element** — the element whose scroll position SSGOI should preserve across transitions. Often a `<main>` or a centered content container.
2. **Apply `relative z-0` (and optionally `overflow-x-clip`) to the element that wraps `<Ssgoi>`.**
3. **Wrap each page in `<SsgoiTransition id="...">`** (see the next section).

Why those classes:

| Class | Why |
|-------|-----|
| `relative` | OUT page is cloned with `position: absolute` — needs a positioned ancestor |
| `z-0` | Creates a stacking context so the OUT page doesn't fall behind backgrounds |
| `overflow-x-clip` | Prevents horizontal overflow flashing during slide/drill (only needed if you use horizontal transitions) |

The scroll element and the `<Ssgoi>` wrapper are typically **the same element**, so all four classes (`overflow-y-auto relative z-0 overflow-x-clip`) sit together.

### Layout example (mobile-style web app)

The library is most often used to ship app-like, mobile-width experiences, so this example shows that shape — a centered max-width column where the column itself scrolls. Adapt as needed for desktop layouts.

```tsx
// src/app/layout.tsx
import { Ssgoi } from "@ssgoi/react";
import { drill, fade } from "@ssgoi/react/view-transitions";

const config = {
  transitions: [
    drill({ enter: "/post/*", exit: "*", type: "parallax" }),
    fade({ paths: ["/", "/about"] }),
  ],
};

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html>
      <body>
        <div className="mx-auto max-w-md h-dvh flex flex-col">
          <main className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto relative z-0 overflow-x-clip">
            <Ssgoi config={config}>
              {children}
            </Ssgoi>
          </main>
          {/* Optional: <BottomNav /> outside <main>, fixed-positioned */}
        </div>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

---

## Page Setup

Wrap each page with `SsgoiTransition`:

```tsx
// app/page.tsx
import { SsgoiTransition } from "@ssgoi/react";

export default function HomePage() {
  return (
    <SsgoiTransition id="/">
      <div>Home content</div>
    </SsgoiTransition>
  );
}

// app/post/[id]/page.tsx
export default function PostPage({ params }: { params: { id: string } }) {
  return (
    <SsgoiTransition id={`/post/${params.id}`}>
      <div>Post content</div>
    </SsgoiTransition>
  );
}
```

---

## SsgoiConfig

```ts
type SsgoiConfig = {
  // Path-matched transitions. Each entry can be a single { from, to, transition }
  // or an array returned by a transition factory (drill, fade, etc.). Arrays are
  // flattened automatically — no spread needed.
  transitions?: (SsgoiPathTransition | SsgoiPathTransition[])[];

  // Rewrite (from, to) before matching. Useful for stripping prefixes/locales.
  middleware?: (from: string, to: string) => { from: string; to: string };

  // Scroll preservation. Defaults are sensible — see section below.
  preserveScroll?: PreserveScrollOption;
};
```

### Transition factory API (6.0)

Each transition factory returns a `SsgoiPathTransition[]`. Drop the result straight into `transitions` — it'll be flattened:

```ts
const config = {
  transitions: [
    drill({ enter: "/post/*", exit: "*" }),       // directional pair
    fade({ paths: ["/", "/about", "/contact"] }), // symmetric N×N
    slide({ paths: ["/tabs/a", "/tabs/b"] }),     // ordered (forward/back)
    zoom({ paths: ["/grid", "/photo/*"], type: "expand" }), // requires data keys
  ],
};
```

Three shapes:

- **`{ paths }`** — symmetric: every pair animates with the same physics. Used by `fade`, `blind`, `film`, `hero`, `jaemin`, `rotate`, `strip`, `zoom`.
- **`{ enter, exit, type? }`** — directional: enter and exit get different physics. Used by `drill`, `sheet`.
- **`{ paths, ... }` with forward/backward variants** — ordered: path order decides direction. Used by `slide`, `scroll`, and `axis`.

All factories accept the unified v6 schema `{ paths (or enter/exit), type?, variant?, options? }`. `type` / `variant` / `options` slots are present on every preset for forward compatibility, even when only one value is implemented today.

### preserveScroll

**Defaults work out of the box.** Mobile viewports automatically preserve scroll position across transitions; desktop does not. You normally don't need to configure this.

**Customizing — exclude specific paths:**

```ts
const config = {
  preserveScroll: { exclude: ["/post/*"] },
};
```

When navigating *to* a path matching `exclude`, the destination starts at scroll position 0. All other navigations keep their preserved scroll.

> **Note:** `skipAnimationOnBack` was removed in 6.0. Native swipe-back gestures are now auto-detected and animations skipped automatically on iOS.

---

## Transitions

Catalog of built-in transitions. Open the linked page for the full signature, options, and (when required) the `data-*` keys to put on your DOM.

### `drill` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/drill.txt
iOS-style hierarchical navigation. New page slides in from the right; old page eases left underneath. **Two types**: `parallax` (depth layering, default) and `slide` (flat cross-faded slide). Use for **List → Detail** flows. (Legacy `type: "crossfade"` deprecated → use `"slide"`.)

### `fade` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/fade.txt
Calm cross-fade between pages. No motion, just opacity. Use as a **safe default** for unrelated pages.

### `slide` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/slide.txt
Horizontal push. Forward navigation slides left, backward slides right. Use for **tab navigation** or sequential page flows.

### `scroll` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/scroll.txt
Vertical "page scroll" — pages slide along the y-axis. **Two types**: `directional` (forward up / backward down, default) and `non-directional` (always slides up regardless of direction). Use for **onboarding** or paginated long-form pages.

### `axis` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/axis.txt
Material/Flutter-style shared-axis page swap. **Three types**: `x` (horizontal, default), `y` (vertical), `z` (depth). On `x`, `variant: "default"` is a relaxed fluid feel and `variant: "snappy"` is a tight tab-swap (KakaoTalk-style). Use for **sibling/tab routes**.

### `sheet` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/sheet.txt
Bottom sheet style. New page slides up from below. **Two types**: `static` (background untouched, default) and `scale` (background scales down behind). Use for **modal-like** flows (FAB → compose, "new item" screens). (Legacy `type: "background-scale"` deprecated → use `"scale"`.)

### `hero` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/hero.txt
Shared element transition. The same logical object (thumbnail, avatar) is tweened in size and position from one page to the next. **Requires matching `data-hero-key` on both pages.**

### `zoom` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/zoom.txt
Card-to-detail expansion. The tapped card grows to fill the detail viewport. **Three types**: `static` (morphs to target size only, default), `expand` (fills viewport), `blur` (background blurs while card focuses). Optional `variant: "fade"` cross-fades surrounding content. **Requires `data-zoom-exit-key` (outgoing) and `data-zoom-enter-key` (incoming)** matching by value.

### `strip` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/strip.txt
3D Y-axis perspective flip. Pages rotate horizontally with depth perspective. Use for **carded, distinctive page swaps** where slide feels too flat.

### `blind` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/blind.txt
Vertical/horizontal blinds wipe across, revealing the new page in staggered slats. **Two types**: `horizontal` (default) and `vertical`. Use for **cinematic, dramatic** reveals.

### `film` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/film.txt
Film-strip style: outgoing page scales down and slides off while incoming scales up from a tile with animated corner borders. Use for **gallery / lightbox** style flows that should feel premium.

### `rotate` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/rotate.txt
Card flip. Outgoing rotates 180° and fades; incoming counter-rotates in from -180°. Use for **playful** transitions between sibling pages.

### `jaemin` — https://ssgoi.dev/llms/jaemin.txt
Quirky: incoming page rotates in at 45° from tiny scale, then unwinds and grows. Use sparingly for **special / playful** moments — modal openings, easter-egg transitions.

---

## Troubleshooting

### Page jumps during transition
- **Cause**: Missing `position: relative` on container
- **Fix**: Add `relative` to the element wrapping `<Ssgoi>`

### OUT page disappears behind background
- **Cause**: Missing `z-index: 0` on container
- **Fix**: Add `z-0` to the div wrapping `{children}`

### Horizontal overflow during slide/drill transitions
- **Cause**: Missing overflow clip
- **Fix**: Add `overflow-x-clip` to container

### Transition not applying
- **Cause**: `id` prop doesn't match route pattern
- **Fix**: Ensure `SsgoiTransition id` matches the actual route path used in `from`/`to`/`paths`

### hero / zoom transition not running
- **Cause**: Data attribute keys don't match between pages, or attribute missing on one side
- **Fix**: For `hero`, both sides use `data-hero-key="<same-value>"`. For `zoom`, outgoing uses `data-zoom-exit-key` and incoming uses `data-zoom-enter-key` (same value)

---

## How It Works (For Debugging)

When a route changes, SSGOI orchestrates two simultaneous animations:
- **OUT**: The leaving page animates out
- **IN**: The entering page animates in

### Core Mechanism: Clone & Absolute Position

When a page unmounts, SSGOI clones it back into the DOM with `position: absolute` so it can animate out while the new page animates in.

```ts
// Internal behavior (packages/core/src/lib/utils/prepare-outgoing.ts)
export const prepareOutgoing = (element, context) => {
  element.style.position = "absolute";  // Removed from flow
  element.style.width = "100%";
  element.style.top = `${-1 * (context?.scrollOffset?.y ?? 0)}px`;
  element.style.left = "0";
};
```

**Why this matters:**
- The OUT page is re-inserted into DOM as a clone with `position: absolute`
- It needs a positioned ancestor (`relative`) to stay in place
- Without proper CSS setup, the OUT page will jump to the wrong position

### Transition Flow

```
/home -> /about navigation:

1. User clicks link to /about
2. /home page unmounts from React
3. SSGOI clones /home and re-inserts it with position: absolute (OUT)
4. React renders /about page (IN)
5. Both pages animate simultaneously
6. Animation complete, cloned /home removed from DOM
```
